one_liner: Clean-room C reimplementation of Apple's closed LZBITMAP codec; format compatibility only, self-described as much slower than Apple's.
what_it_does: Decodes and encodes Apple's LZBITMAP format (magic 'ZBM\x09'), which APFS uses for compressed extended attributes and resource forks and which Apple ships without source. The API is three C functions in libzbitmap.h: zbm_decompress, zbm_compress and zbm_compress_chunk, all buffer-to-buffer with explicit destination sizes and negative error codes (ZBM_NOMEM, ZBM_INVAL, ZBM_RANGE, ZBM_OVERFLOW). Passing a NULL destination returns the decompressed length or the worst-case compressed length.
how_it_is_fast: It is not a speed play. Data is cut into 32 KiB chunks; each 8-byte group is coded as an 8-bit bitmap saying which bytes are literal and which are copied from a fixed back-distance ('period'), with the 12 most frequent bitmaps stored in a 17-byte trailer, the rest in a metadata area and runs of the same bitmap number nibble-coded. The decoder works one byte at a time with a bounds check per byte, and the encoder scans up to 255 earlier positions per 8-byte group, plus memchr-guided candidates up to 64 KiB back, so throughput is low; the only speed lever is zbm_compress_chunk, which lets callers compress chunks on several threads.
when_to_use: Reading LZBITMAP-compressed files or xattrs from APFS volumes or iOS 16+ images on non-Apple platforms, where Apple's libcompression is unavailable.
Producing LZBITMAP output that must round-trip through this library's own decoder (for example in filesystem tooling tests).
Embedding a small, dependency-free MIT decoder in a C or C++ tool; the decoder is about 440 lines and is already reused in the linux-apfs-rw kernel module.
when_not_to_use: As a general-purpose fast compressor: the README says it is much slower than Apple's original, and there is no benchmark at all against lz4, zstd or lzfse.
When you control the format: LZ4 or zstd give better speed, ratio and tooling, and LZFSE has an open reference implementation from Apple.
For untrusted input through the size query: a NULL-destination zbm_decompress call on a crafted header can hang (see gotchas).
Where long-term maintenance matters: 11 commits between 2022-11-22 and 2023-01-18, no releases, no issues filed, no fuzzing or CI in the repo.
If you need encoder output certified as decodable by Apple's own implementation: test/test.c only checks Apple-made files decode correctly and that its own output round-trips through its own decoder.

integration.form: static lib (two source files: libzbitmap.c and libzbitmap.h; Makefile builds libzbitmap.a)
integration.dependencies: none (libc only; the test program uses pthreads)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 with GNU extensions (Makefile uses gcc --std=gnu99 -O3 -fno-strict-aliasing)
integration.platforms: any with a C compiler; the encoder's unaligned uint64_t loads assume a target that tolerates them (x86-64, arm64), and its match-cost heuristic assumes little-endian byte order
integration.thread_safety: Reentrant: no global state, each compress call callocs its own roughly 25 KB state; zbm_compress_chunk is designed to be called from several threads on the same source buffer.

gotchas: Hang on crafted input: with dest == NULL, zbm_handle_chunk returns before checking that the chunk length is at least the 6-byte header, so a chunk with len 0 and a nonzero decompressed length makes the zbm_decompress loop add 0 to src forever. The kernel port in linux-apfs-rw carries the same loop; whether its callers use the NULL query was not checked. Size queries on untrusted data should be avoided or capped.

The encoder reads candidate matches with *(uint64_t *) casts at unaligned addresses (undefined behaviour in ISO C; it relies on -fno-strict-aliasing and on hardware that tolerates unaligned loads). zbm_compress_chunk also leaks its calloc'd state when the index overflows (it returns ZBM_OVERFLOW before free).

Chunks may reference data from earlier chunks (back-distances up to 0xffff across chunk boundaries), so zbm_compress_chunk must be given the whole source buffer and the full output must be decoded in order into one contiguous buffer.
Compressed output from zbm_compress_chunk must be concatenated in index order by the caller, and the stream ends with a 6-byte empty chunk (ZBM_LAST_CHUNK_SIZE); out_len is not written on error.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only when the data is already LZBITMAP (APFS/iOS); for anything you encode yourself, LZFSE (Apple's open-source codec) or LZ4 are faster and better documented, and zstd gives a better ratio.
verified_claims_summary: No measurement exists: the README's only statement is that the reimplementation is 'much slower than the original' Apple LZBITMAP with similar ratios, and test/test.c reports compression ratio and correctness only, with no timing.
status_note: Abandoned since 2023-01-18 (last commit 'Add a license', MIT, 58 stars), but its decoder lives on, ported under GPL-2.0+ OR MIT, in linux-apfs-rw and in a 2025 staging RFC for an in-kernel APFS driver; small enough to vendor.
